editorial.headline: The Quiet Machinery of a Working Facility
editorial.standfirst: Although open nationally to 100% foreign ownership, this facility-support activity cannot be registered for PMA in Bali today.
editorial.body:
Facility support becomes a distinct business when it is supplied as a combined operational service within a client’s premises. The work can bring together general interior cleaning, maintenance, waste disposal, doorman duties, monitoring, mail delivery, reception, laundry and related services that support the facility’s operations. Rather than selling a single task in isolation, the activity concerns a coordinated package: people on site performing the practical work that helps the client’s facility function from one day to the next. It is an infrastructure of everyday operations, assembled around the place where the client works.

That operational role also establishes its boundary. The provider supplies staff to perform these supporting services, but does not become involved in, or assume responsibility for, the client’s main business or activity. It is not a mandate to manage and operate the client’s entire enterprise, and the record also makes clear that the offering is not simply one support service supplied alone. The service’s practical character is inseparable from that division of responsibility: combined support is delivered inside the client facility, in service of the client’s own operations.

Who may enter the activity is equally clear in the national record. It is open at Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scales, placing the same combined-service proposition across the stated business scales. For PMA, its status is TERBUKA and the stated foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%. The PMA source is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. On the national position alone, then, the record permits foreign ownership up to the whole of that stated ceiling.

But national openness is not the final word in Bali. The record places the activity in BLOCCATO_CLASSE_RISCHIO: at the Besar scale, every listed scope is OSS-rated Rendah or Menengah-Rendah, triggering the Bali moratorium dated May 13, 2026. The provincial rule is unambiguous: all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI are blocked for PMA, island-wide and permanently. A foreign investor therefore cannot register this activity for PMA in Bali today. The result is not a smaller local ownership allowance: nationally the ceiling remains 100%, while Bali’s PMA-registration outcome is blocked.
